packet-05 - unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this packet. I followed the brief; I opened only the brief, PROMPT.md and image files in the packet directory.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)

Observations:
- One photograph of five separate parchment fragments on a black ground, with a cm ruler at top and a colour checker at lower right. Pencil shelfmark labels on each piece: "Stams, STA, Frg. 47_1r" (large upper-left piece), "47_3r" (upper-right strip), "47_2r" (lower-left strip), "47_4r" (lower-middle strip), "47_5r" (lower-right strip). All appear upright.
- 47_1r (upper left, large): a largely blank/stained leaf with vertical ruling; written text survives in two areas: (a) a narrow column on the left side, partly under/through old transparent tape and grey residue, many short lines of a Gothic textualis-type hand, left edge cut away; (b) a short block near the top centre/right of about 13-14 lines in a smaller, more formal hand, apparently liturgical prayer text (I can see words like "oblata", "corpore", "pro" endings "p(er) d(omi)n(u)m"); the rest of the page below is blank but ruled. There is an irregular cut-out shape at lower left and a separate small strip below.
- 47_3r (upper right): a vertical strip, single column, about 40 lines of a dense small Gothic cursive/bastarda-like hand with red touches (rubricated initials/paraphs, some red strokes on capitals). Right edge clipped; text runs to the edge. Small marginal mark at left (around line 13-14).
- 47_2r (lower left): narrow vertical strip, single column, about 45 lines, text cut at both left and right edges; red highlighting on some capitals.
- 47_4r (lower middle): narrow strip, single column; red paraphs/initials; a gap with a larger red-touched initial (looks like "Allegabat iesus"?) near mid-height after the shelfmark label - the piece may be two fragments or a column with a section break.
- 47_5r (lower right): strip of about 45 lines single column in a Gothic hand, with three marginal notes in the right margin (at about lines 3-5, about 21-22, and about 34-36), written smaller.

Tentative interpretation: the strips (2r-5r) are offcuts from one or more manuscripts of prose (sermons/theological text?), single-column; 1r carries a liturgical prayer block. Not inferring work or date.

The overview is too small to read; readings below come from tiles only.

====================================================================
image-002.jpg - native tile, upper part of Frg. 47_1r (top ~2/3 of the leaf)
====================================================================
Layout seen in this tile: two written areas. LEFT: a narrow column (ruled
both sides) of small Gothic text, left edge of each line cut/damaged, top
under old clear tape (grey). Continues below the tile. RIGHT (beyond a blank
ruled column): a block of 14 lines at the top, rest of that column blank.
Small marginal "2" next to right block lines 8 and 13 (line-ending marks?),
and a pencil/ink "2" and "3" far left on the blank margin. Line numbers
below are my count of text lines from the top of the image.

LEFT COLUMN (subject: ecclesiastical grades; each line begins cut):

002 L02  [illegible, under tape]

002 L34  hibuit [illegible, cut at bottom of tile]

Note on "x̄(?)": after "hunc" the scribe repeatedly writes a sign like a
looped x/z with a stroke; I cannot settle whether it is the et-sign or a
nomen sacrum (x(ristu)s); left unexpanded.

Below R14: blank ruled parchment to the bottom of the tile.

====================================================================
image-003.jpg - native tile, right part of Frg. 47_1r + upper Frg. 47_3r
====================================================================
Overlap: the left half repeats the right prayer block of 47_1r already
read on image-002 (R01-R14); not re-transcribed. New on this part: at the
right edge of 47_1r, at about 82% of tile height, a small marginal note
in a later(?) hand, struck through in red: "indic(?) p[...]" (cut by edge).
A strip of clear tape at that edge.

Frg. 47_3r: single column, Gothic cursive (bastarda-like), red strokes on
capitals and red paraphs/initials. Right edge cut, so line ends lost.
Left margin note at lines 14-15: "2a" over "2" over "a"(?) (small, pale).
Red "2a" also inside the text at right end of line 13. Lines numbered
from top of the strip as seen here (34 lines visible; continues below).
